newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes climb late, trailing gasoline.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes climb late, trailing gasoline.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices climbed late Thursday, trailing the upward path of NYMEX gasoline that was spurred by short covering ahead of Friday's contract expiry, traders said.
March West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was trading around $24.75-85 a barrel, up 30 cents from late Wednesday's cash market, traders said.
The March/April WTI spread was around 47 cents, while the corresponding WTI//Cushing Posting Plus changed hands at $2.38 and $2.40 a barrel, up two to four cents from the highest deal on Wednesday.
The grades were generally weaker in light activity.
WTI/Midland was done at 35-39 cents under WTI/Cushing, down from 31-35 cents on Wednesday.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St.James traded at WTI/Cushing plus 20-23 cents a barrel, up from 17-19 cents on Wednesday.
West Texas Sour/Midland was done at $2.03 and also in an unconfirmed deal at $2.08, down around 20 cents from Wednesday.
